BLOCKER: No test persists a valid design pack; AC-1 "persists a valid design pack" is unproven (only malformed/auth paths tested).
No test covers stale-revision rejection (`expected_revision`/`_guard_revision`) despite it being an explicit AC-1 clause.
No test covers missing-operator-role rejection (403); only anonymous 401 is tested, so the role boundary is unverified.
MAJOR: Pack validation is reimplemented inline in the router (dict-nonempty, controls-list only) instead of reusing the canonical `scripts/dev/design_pack.py` validator, risking rule drift from the design contract's required row fields.
OpenAPI advertises only 200/422; `ApiError` outcomes (400/401/403/409) are undocumented, so clients cannot distinguish malformed pack vs stale revision vs forbidden.
`require_operator` is declared twice (route `dependencies` and `ctx: Depends(...)`) with `ctx` unused — redundant boundary wiring that can mask intent during future authz changes.
MINOR: Handler imports `core.backlog` inline instead of at module top, inconsistent with import conventions and hard to trace for dependency analysis.
No log/metric emitted on write, validation failure, or stale-revision rejection (guardrail: minimum observability to diagnose failure).
Request body schema is untyped `additionalProperties: true`, so the OpenAPI contract gives consumers no field-level validation guidance.
NIT: Default scope string `"product_forge"` is hardcoded in the handler; centralize with other route scope defaults.
Test wrapper's `assert _loaded > 0` fails opaquely if the canonical test file is renamed/moved.
SUMMARY: Endpoint reuses `core.backlog.update` (no duplicate store) and is published in OpenAPI, satisfying AC-2 structurally, but AC-1 is not demonstrated: persistence, stale-revision, and operator-role behaviors lack tests.
Top risks: untested authz/revision boundaries and router-local validation that can drift from the canonical design-pack validator.
